 1. Ram Sogarath Yadav S/o Late Charan Yadav Resident of Village- Dekuli,
 PS- Bhadurpur, Distt.- Darbhanga, Bihar  2. Anita Devi W/o Ram Sogarath Yadav R/o vill - Dekuli, P.S.- Bhadurpur,

sentences.text: Versus
1 . The State of Bihar  2. Bachandeo Prasad S/o Ram Sewak Yadav R/o Sisho West, P.S.- Sadar  (Mabbi OP), Distt.- Darbhanga, Bihar

Respondent/s  ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Mr.Prakash Chandra, Adv.
 For the State : Mrs.Anita Kumari Singh, APP  For the Respondent no.2 : Mr.Sunil Kumar Karn, Adv.
 ======================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR SINGH  ORAL ORDER 5 02-02-2026 1-Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for the informant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor representing the State.
2-This appeal under Section 415 read with section 430 of the B.N.S.S., 2023 has been preferred by the appellants namely Ram Sogarath Yadav and Anita Devi against the judgment of conviction dated 28.05.2025 and order of sentence dated 12.06.2025 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-XI, Darbhanga, in Sessions Trial No.29 of 2022, arising out of Bahadurpur Police Station Case No.45 of 2021, under sections 498A/307/34 of the IPC and section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Patna High Court CR.

(b) Six months' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.
5000/- for the offence under Section 498A/34 of the IPC.

sentences.text: (c) Six months' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.25000/- for the offence u/s 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for three months.
All the sentences are ordered to run concurrently.
3-The appellants have prayed for suspension of their sentence and release on bail during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal before this Court.

4-As per the prosecution case in brief, complainant alleged that his daughter was married with Monu Kumar Yadav on 30.01.2020 and for marriage expenses, complainant deposited an amount of Rs.3,01,000/- in the account of Monu Kumar Yadav.
He also gave furniture, household goods and jewellery of gold and silver in the marriage.

It is alleged that after one month of marriage, Monu Kumar Yadav, Ram Sogarath Yadav (father-in-law of the victim), Anita Devi Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2881 of 2025(5) dt.02-02-2026 (mother-in-law of the victim) and other accused persons started demanding Rs.5,00,000/- as dowry, where upon, the complainant gave Rs.2,00,000/- to his son-in-law for business but they continued their demand for dowry and on non- fulfillment of the same, they used to torture the complainant's daughter.
On 16.01.2021 at about 11:15 AM, Monu Kumar Yadav called the complainant on his mobile and told that his daughter has been burnt and asked him to send the vehicle.

When the complainant reached there,
he saw that his daughter was burnt above waist and was crying in pain, hence, he took her to the hospital, where she disclosed that all the four persons asked for dowry and on refusal they threatened to kill her.
It is alleged that Monu Kumar Yadav and Ramsogarath Yadav caught her and Chandan Yadav poured kerosene oil on her body and Anita Devi matched a stick and put fire due to which she got severely burnt.
5- Learned counsel for the appellants argued that the appellants are innocent and have been falsely implicated in this case.
Impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence of the appellants is not sustainable in the eyes of the law.
Appellant no.1 is the father-in-law of the victim and appellant no.2 is the mother-in-law of the victim.

Apart from merit of the case much Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.2881 of 2025(5) dt.02-02-2026 emphasis has been given by contending that the maximum sentence awarded to the appellants is up to five years and they are in jail since 19.04.2021 as such, till date, appellants have served incarceration of about 4 years and 9 months, therefore,
considering the detention period of the appellants, they may be released on bail.
Lastly, it is submitted that on account of huge pendency of cases before this Court, there is no likelihood of the appeal being heard in near future.
In case appellants is granted bail, they will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in early hearing of this appeal.

6-Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 as well as learned A.P.P. though opposed the prayer for bail of the appellants by contending that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubts, hence at this stage presumption of innocence is not available to the appellants.

7-Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as looking to the detention period of the appellants in jail as mentioned above, I find that they have made out a case for grant of bail in the light of judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Saudan Singh vs. State of U.P., 2021 SCC OnLine SC 3259, wherein, it Ram Sogarath Yadav vs The State Of Bihar on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100609949/
2 has been observed by the Apex Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: APP (SJ) No.2881 of 2025(5) dt.02-02-2026 Court that there may be even convicts in custody in cases other than life sentence cases and in those cases again the broad parameter of 50 percent of the actual sentence undergone can be the basis for grant of bail and in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I, (2022) 10 SCC 51 wherein, it has been observed inter-alia that when a person has undergone detention for a period extending to one- half of the maximum period of imprisonment specified for that offence, he shall be released by the court on his personal bond with or without sureties.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. C.B.I, (2022) 10 SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
8-The Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Atul @ Ashutosh versus State of Madhya Pradesh also while allowing Criminal Appeal No. 579 of 2024 vide order dated 02.02.2024 has made following observations:-
"Before parting with order, we must note here that notwithstanding several decisions of this Court holding that when there is a fixed term sentence and especially when the appeal is not likely to be heard before completing entire period of sentence, normally suspension of sentence and bail should be granted.

entities.text: Atul @ Ashutosh versus State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We find that in several deserving cases, bail is being denied.
Such cases should never be required to be brought before this Court".

9-Hence, without expressing any opinion on the merit of Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.2881 of 2025(5) dt.02-02-2026 the case, the sentence of the appellants is suspended during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal.

10-Let the appellants- Ram Sogarath Yadav and Anita Devi be enlarged on bail during pendency of this appeal in above Case on his furnishing bail bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned subject to deposit of 50% amount fine.
The realization of remaining 50% amount of fine shall remain stayed till disposal of this Criminal Appeal.
11-On acceptance of the bail bonds, the concerned Court below shall furnish the photocopy thereof to this Court for being kept on record of this Criminal Appeal.
12-Let this Criminal Appeal be listed in due course for hearing.
